background.n37: Measured on 2026-10-17 after the law was committed, but not entered in a ledger beforehand: three soups gave period 262143 (the law); a column-constant start gave 87381 (rule 90's published value). It is not part of this test.
background.prior_work: McLaughlin (West Chester) lists the periods of this rule on odd tori up to 23, as a conjecture; Martin, Odlyzko and Wolfram (1984) proved the analogous structure for 1D rule 90, which first falls short of 2^sord - 1 at n = 37.

design.cap: 2 * law(n) + n + 10 generations, so a period up to twice the law is seen
design.selection:
The sizes tested, by a rule fixed before the run: every n from 36 to 100 that is not a
power of 2 and whose predicted period costs at most BUDGET cell-generations, except 37, which
was measured on 2026-10-17 before this ledger existed.

starts.columns: seed 1: a random column vector repeated along y (constant in y), which evolves exactly as rule 90 on the n-cycle
starts.soup: random soup at the density, one per seed

body.title: Periods of B1357/S1357 on n x n square tori, n = 36..100

body.decision: confirmed at n when the longest period over the three soups equals the prediction; refuted at n when any soup's period does not divide it (a period above it, or an unsettled run, does not divide it); short at n when every period divides it but none equals it
